text:
emma: quick check — we keep hitting edgecases where late-arriving tokens rewrite attribution and blow up downstream billing joins. thinking out loud about a minimal boundary between ingest and accounting so backfills don't require massive replay
raj: ugh same. current ingest hands an enriched envelope to the ledger, but the finalization step still tries to mutate ownership which is the problem
sophia: can you sketch the mutation path? is it a replace-on-late-arrival or append-with-adjust?
emma: right now it's replace-if-newer-timestamp. but invoices assume append-only proofs. when a late event replaces an ownership claim it invalidates assertions for already-issued charge batches
mike: two quick options: 1) make ingest emit compensating "adjustment" events (append-only) so downstream can apply deltas; 2) move all final ownership resolution into a reconciler that outputs immutable audit-records for billing
raj: option 1 keeps ingest simple but makes every consumer smart about applying deltas. option 2 centralizes complexity but adds latency 
emma: tradeoffs: append-only adjustments: lower latency for ingest, higher complexity for every consumer (billing, reports). reconciler: single source of truth but you introduce a reconciliation window and potential billing delay
sophia: could we hybrid? ingest writes candidate_claim records to a short-lived table, emits a proto-event with provenance pointer. reconciler reads candidates, emits canonicalized ownership events into the append-only ledger once stable. consumers only read ledger for billing
mike: hybrid sounds sensible. questions: what does "stable" mean? sequence number? watermark? policy TTL?
raj: pragmatic: watermark + change-window. if no conflicting candidate arrives for X minutes or past watermark advance, reconciler seals. we already have watermark logic for ingestion acking, reuse it
emma: also need a cheap way to surface "provenance pointers" inside audit events so audit tooling can reconstruct candidate history. something like provenance_id + candidate_snapshots S3 path
sophia: +1. audit tooling needs full chain for disputes. include minimal metadata on event (provenance_id, candidate_versions_count, reconcile_policy) and put full snapshot in backing store
mike: implementation note: keep ledger write idempotent => use deterministic event_id: sha256(provenance_id || reconciliation_epoch). consumer can de-dupe easily
raj: example event shape (very small):
```json
{"event_id":"<sha>", "tenant":"acme", "timestamp":"2026-03-21T15:00:00Z", "ownership":[{"account":"acct-1","tokens":123}], "provenance_id":"pv_abc123", "provenance_s3":"s3://redwood-provenance/pv_abc123.json"}
```
emma: Sounds good. operational concerns: reconciler needs to be highly observable (why a claim sealed), and we need SLA for reconcilers in Dedicated deployments
sophia: failure modes: reconciler lag -> billing missing rows (delay). reconciler crash during epoch -> ensure durable checkpoints and re-run idempotently. make reconcile epoch atomic and resumable
mike: infra-bot: scheduled job started: reconcile-run-2026-03-21T15:00Z :white_check_mark:
raj: security note: provenance snapshots may include sensitive prompt metadata. ensure snapshots are encrypted and access-controlled. we can strip PII before storing but keep enough for audit
emma: next steps: prototyping candidate table + reconciler in staging. I'll open a short RFC with sequence diagrams and expected metrics (reconcile latency, extra storage, cost per tenant). any objections?
sophia: no objections. suggest we also add a "safety-fallback" where if reconciler falls behind beyond threshold, ingest can emit a temporarily safe fallback event (coarse-grained cost attribution) so billing keeps flowing
mike: agreed. i'll add a small proposal for the fallback policy and SLA alerts
emma: thanks team — i'll post RFC link when drafted. ping me if you want to pair on the reconciler checkpointing design
